rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.

Checked every pronoun/demonstrative/named artifact against prior chunks and against the M3 exercise set. 'the test-strategy skill' (chunk 3, line 19) is the compendium's own worked example of module-include-order vocabulary. 'the delta note' (chunk 5, line 31) resolves against curriculum/exercises/map-the-access-surface.md line 135 ('Writes a delta note that names one surface...'). 'The one-threat pick' / 'the STRIDE walk' (chunk 5, line 31) resolve against curriculum/exercises/threat-model-with-stride.md (titled 'Pick one threat, record the decision'; 'Save the map and the STRIDE walk before you clear'). 'The side quest' (chunk 6, line 36) resolves against curriculum/exercises/open-the-side-quest.md. Every law coming up' (chunk 1, line 7) is a forward pointer to the deck's own remaining structure, not an unnamed content referent.

No cross-file callback found; module references (M1, M2, M4) name modules by name, not position, and are the file's own §3-carved arc subject (this lecture's whole job is naming the M1-M3 arc). No 'the prior lecture' / 'as we said before' shaped pointers.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal structure in this file; it is a pure consolidation/recognition closer with no live-demo beat.

Harm: a slide with no self-carrying claim projects as empty air. Every chunk (1-7) carries at least one complete, self-standing claim with mechanism, not just a wait-state bullet. Closest case: chunk 1 leads with scene-setting before 'One loop, three sizes' lands the claim — still self-carrying within the chunk.

Harm: a header the chunk's own content contradicts misleads a skim-reader. Checked all 7 headers against their chunk content: 'Back to the map: near half filled' -> chunk fills in near-half names; 'The loop and the model it runs on' -> agent loop + context-files-as-model; 'How the loop compounds' -> compound ladder + double-loop learning; 'The governor you carry forward' -> governor definition; 'Reading was never the control' -> control-is-interrogation argument; 'The branch is the permission' -> branch-scoped autonomy argument; 'The far half goes quiet' -> far half loses fast feedback. All true summaries.

Harm: cadence tics read as filler on a projected slide. Checked each sub-item: no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction anywhere in body. No anaphora/epistrophe triple with an empty third leg (chunk 4's 'It prices... picks... tells you' has three distinct concrete legs, not a triple-repeat cadence). No self-grading superlative (chunk 5's 'the biggest yet' is a factual size comparison across modules, not a training-usefulness claim -- closest case to a violation, stays inside because it grades the student's own output size, not the training). No number-with-retraction pair. No abstraction-noun stack. No empty-leg verb triplet (chunk 5's 'Ranked list first, probe where you know most, make the output name its weak spot' -- three concrete, distinct actions, none fails 'what does this concretely mean?').

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: over-bolding trains the reader to stop trusting bold as a signal. This is a law-consolidation closer, where the rule allows one handle per law. Counted bolds per chunk: chunk1=1 ('One loop, three sizes'), chunk2=2 (one per law: 'closed-loop controller', 'Local success, global drift'), chunk3=2 (one per law: 'The compound ladder', 'Double-loop learning'), chunk4=2 ('A governor is a pre-action question', 'Name the uncertainty before you move' -- both explicitly logged as kept in the file's own 2026-07-09 emphasis-pass maintainer note), chunk5=1 ('Control is interrogation'), chunk6=0, chunk7=0. Every bold is a ≲5-word handle naming a coined term/law, never a whole sentence. Matches the file's dated, Antti-directed emphasis pass exactly.
